caption:

threads_text: Base44, the app builder Wix bought for about $80 million, lets you describe an app in plain English and get logins, a database and hosting without writing code. The free plan gives you 25 message credits a month. What is the first app you would build with it?

slides.headline: How to use *Base44* to build a working app for free

slides.heading: 1. Describe the *app*
paras: On the Base44 home screen, say who the app is for, what it helps them do and why it is useful.
Keep the first prompt to the core idea. Add details later.

slides.heading: 2. Plan *before* you build
paras: Pick Plan in the mode menu beside Build. Base44 asks about your users, the main flows and the design.
Plan messages cost a fraction of a credit. The first build costs about 1.

slides.heading: 3. Fix it *one piece* at a time
paras: The AI chat sits on the left, your live app on the right. Ask for one change per message.
Select mode lets you click an element and edit it directly, with no credits used.

slides.heading: 4. Hit *Publish*
paras: Click Publish in the top bar, then share the link.
Free gives you 25 message credits a month, at most 5 a day, and up to 5 apps. Spend them on real changes.

slides.hook: Follow for guides that turn AI tools into things you can actually ship.

site_article.headline: How to use Base44 to build an app for free
site_article.dek: A step by step walkthrough of Base44, the AI app builder owned by Wix: how to write the first prompt, use Plan mode, refine without wasting credits, publish, and what the Free plan really covers.
site_article.summary: Base44 builds a working app, with logins, a database and hosting, from a plain language description. Its Free plan includes 25 message credits a month, up to 5 a day, and up to 5 apps.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Base44 to build an app for free (step by step)
site_article.seo_description: How to use Base44 step by step: write the first prompt, use Plan mode, refine and publish your app, plus 4 prompts to copy and the Free plan's 25 credit limit.
site_article.answer_summary: Sign up at Base44, describe who your app is for and what it does, or use Plan mode first, then refine it in the AI chat and click Publish. The Free plan gives 25 message credits a month, at most 5 a day, for up to 5 apps.
site_article.hero_alt: Screenshot of the Base44 home screen with a prompt box set to Build.

paragraphs.text: Base44 is an AI app builder: you describe an app in plain language and it builds a working version, including the design, the database, user signups, permissions and hosting, with no code. If you want to know how to use Base44 to build an app for free, the short version is this: sign up, describe your idea, refine it in the AI chat, and click Publish.

Base44 was started by Israeli programmer Maor Shlomo and was about six months old, with roughly 250,000 users, when Wix agreed to buy it for about $80 million in cash on June 18, 2025, according to TechCrunch. Wix said the deal also includes earn out payments through 2029.
How to use Base44: your first build

paragraphs.title: 1. Sign up and write your first prompt
paragraphs.text: After you sign up, the Base44 home screen shows one prompt box. Base44's prompt guide says a good first prompt covers three things: who the app is for, what it helps them do, and why that is useful. Keep it to the heart of the app. You can add every other feature later, and smaller requests also use fewer credits.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A simple first build
paragraphs.text: Build an expense tracker for freelancers who bill several clients. Users log an expense, tag it with a client and a category, and see monthly totals per client on a dashboard. Keep the design clean and calm, with one main page and a simple form.

The AI may ask a few clarifying questions before it builds. You can skip them, or answer with a placeholder like [company name] and fill it in later. There is also speech to text if you would rather talk than type.

paragraphs.title: 2. Use Plan mode when the idea is still fuzzy
paragraphs.text: In the prompt box, open the Mode menu beside Build and choose Plan. Base44 then talks the idea through with you: what the app is for, who uses it and in which roles, the core flows, and the design. When the plan looks right, click Start Building. According to the docs, plan messages cost a fraction of a credit and the first build costs about 1 credit.

paragraphs.title: 3. Start from files, a website or a design if you have one
paragraphs.text: The plus menu on the first prompt offers more ways in. Attach files from your computer or Google Drive: images and PDFs act as a visual reference, while spreadsheets and CSV files shape the data. Start from URL copies a site you own, as Content & Design or Design only. You can also import from Figma or pick connectors such as Google Workspace, Slack or GitHub.
Start from URL does not copy private backend code, hidden data or third party integrations. Use it to rebuild the look and the public content, then add the logic with prompts.
Refine the app without burning credits

paragraphs.title: 4. Learn the editor
paragraphs.text: Once the first version is built, the editor shows the AI chat on the left and a live preview on the right. The top bar holds Edit mode, the Dashboard, version history and the publishing controls. Previewing the app is free; changes made through the chat cost credits based on the work and the model.

paragraphs.title: 5. Ask for one change at a time
paragraphs.text: Base44's own advice is to build in stages: get the core feature working, then add the next piece. Describe what the screen should show, say why, and ask for the fix rather than the flaw. Instead of saying the homepage looks cluttered, ask for fewer items per row and more space between sections.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Describe the screen you want
paragraphs.text: Redesign the dashboard so it shows three cards at the top: total spent this month, number of expenses, and the client with the highest spend. Below them, add a bar chart of spending per month for the last 6 months. I want to see at a glance which client costs me the most.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Add logic, not just looks
paragraphs.text: Only show the Delete button on an expense to the user who created it. When an expense is over [amount], mark it with a red label so it stands out in the list.

paragraphs.title: 6. Use Select mode, Discuss mode and version history
paragraphs.text: Select mode lets you click the exact element you want to change, and direct edits do not use credits. Discuss mode is for brainstorming: it talks through ideas without changing the app, and the docs say it uses fewer credits than building. Version history lets you restore an earlier version, so you can experiment without fear.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 4: Plan a feature in Discuss mode first
paragraphs.text: I want to add a booking flow where clients pick a time slot and get a confirmation email. Before you build anything, list the pages, the data you would store, and the steps a client goes through. Tell me what you would build first.
Test and publish your Base44 app

paragraphs.title: 7. Test it like a real user
paragraphs.text: Click through the preview the way a user would. Under More actions, Act as a user shows the app as a specific person or role. Base44 also suggests opening the app in a private browser window and on a phone. The device menu in the top bar switches the preview to mobile size.

paragraphs.title: 8. Click Publish
paragraphs.text: Click Publish in the top bar. The panel has Web and Mobile app tabs. From there you can edit the web address, share the app, set App visibility, check the Security status, and publish your latest changes. Get domain sets up a custom address. To take an app offline later, go to Dashboard, then Settings, then Danger Zone, then Unpublish App; your data and settings stay.
If the chat shows Thinking for a long time, wait: the docs say detailed prompts can take 10 to 15 minutes. If it stalls, break the request into smaller prompts.
What the Base44 Free plan includes

The Free plan costs nothing and includes 25 message credits a month, with at most 5 a day, 100 integration credits a month, up to 5 apps, and core features such as authentication, a database and analytics. For apps created from October 18, 2026, each app's database is capped at 200 MB.

Some things need a paid plan. Starter, listed at $16 a month billed annually, adds 100 message credits, unlimited apps, custom domains, private apps and the option to hide the Edit with Base44 badge on live apps. Builder, listed at $40 a month billed annually, adds code export to a ZIP file or GitHub, payments through providers like Stripe, and a choice of AI model.

Five message credits a day go fast if you ask for one small tweak per message. On the Free plan, plan in Plan or Discuss mode, write clear requests that cover a whole screen, and use Select mode for small text and style edits. Base44 is a fast way to get a real, working prototype; just do not expect a free app with your own domain, private access or payments.
